Team — forwarding Acme's redlines. Quick read and suggested play: we should aim to close commercial terms without conceding items that materially increase platform risk or cost. My initial priorities:
- Uptime: propose compromise 99.95% rolling monthly with clearly defined measurement window (UTC-based)
- Credits: cap at 10% of monthly bill or three months' aggregated credits, whichever is lower (legal prefers a cap)
- Response SLA: maintain 24/7 P1 response acknowledgement target of 15 minutes for incidents impacting >20% of traffic; otherwise 1 hour. P2 stays 4 hours.
- Maintenance: keep 2x monthly 4-hour windows (we're flexible on scheduling) with 72-hour notice; emergency maintenance exempt with post-facto notification and detailed RCA

Can legal (Soojin) confirm what wording we can offer on credits cap and measurement method? Marissa — will need a delta TCV impact if we accept tighter response windows. Lauren — can you confirm if this bumps the procurement approval path?

I plan to send a compromise proposal back to Acme by EOD Wednesday (6/13).

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi / team,

Reviewed Acme's redlines. High-level legal guidance below — we can push but not accept clauses that remove reasonable caps or create open-ended liability. Specific recommendations: 
- Uptime: counter to 99.95% (monthly, measured by request success across public API endpoints) with explicit exclusions (force majeure, customer-caused degradation, scheduled maintenance). If they insist on 99.99%, require either a higher price tier (dedicated pool) or a defined margin for credits.
- Credits: propose a stepped credit schedule but with a monthly aggregate cap equal to 10% of monthly recurring charges. Remove language that allows unlimited stacking per incident.
- Response times: accept 24/7 P1 ack <= 15 minutes but define "ack" as initial triage commencement (ticket opened + first engineer assigned) and not full remediation. For P2, propose 4 hours. Attach wording for definitions.
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice standard; limit to four maintenance hours per calendar month (or two 4-hour windows), emergency maintenance clause with post-incident notification and RCA within 5 business days.
- Escalation & termination: include cure period language (30 days) for repeated SLA breaches before termination rights escalate.

I'll attach a short excerpt with the exact redline language. If Sales accepts the cap on credits, Legal can sign off quickly. If Acme refuses the cap, we'll need procurement to escalate price/architecture options (Dedicated).

Soojin
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Tim — thanks for the redlines and the clear list of priorities. We appreciate Acme's scale and the mission-critical nature of your use case. After an internal review, here's a compromise we can commit to for the Order Form / SLA: 

Summary of proposed compromises (we hope this shortens the loop):
- Uptime: 99.95% (monthly, rolling) measured on the public inference API endpoints. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, customer configuration issues, force majeure.
- Service credits: stepped credit schedule for monthly uptime below thresholds; aggregate monthly cap = 10% of monthly recurring charges. Credits issued as bill credit only (no cash refunds).
- Response targets: P1 acknowledgement (24/7) within 15 minutes for incidents affecting availability >=20% of traffic; P1 remediation target depends on incident severity and will be handled under our incident response playbook. P2 response target = 4 business hours.
- Maintenance windows: up to two windows per month, up to 4 hours each. We will provide 72 hours' advance notice for planned maintenance. Emergency maintenance is permitted with immediate notification and an RCA delivered within 5 business days.
- If Acme requires 99.99% or removal of the credits cap, we can discuss Dedicated capacity (pricing addendum).

Attached is a proposed order form that embeds these items and highlights legal-friendly language. If this aligns with Acme's needs, can we get confirmation by next Friday (2028-06-17) so procurement can route DocuSign? If there are narrow points, we're happy to jump on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Link to proposed order form and diff: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AexampleAcmeOrderForm

Naomi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
